title: Telemetry data escrow and epochal pruning for tenant compliance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Enable a tenant-first retention and retrieval model for observability streams by implementing a data escrow and epochal pruning layer. The feature must allow long-term legal holds and short-term operational retention to coexist, provide just-in-time rehydration for investigation, and produce tamper-evident audit logs of access. This reduces product-facing surface for PII exposure and simplifies compliance requests without increasing storage costs linearly.
background: Current observability ingestion writes full traces, logs, and metrics to a unified hot store with a single TTL. Customers request mixed retention profiles: 7d for operational traces, 90d for metrics, and indefinite for items under legal hold. Our existing pipelines lack a lightweight mechanism to isolate long-lived events from hot storage and to rehydrate context for incident replay. Previous tickets (see dependencies) implemented redaction and tenant-scoped retention, but do not support selective escrow and epochal pruning with legal hold rehydration.
tasks: Design escrow storage format: compact index + encrypted chunk layout with tenant-scoped keys
Define epoch boundaries and pruning algorithm (epoch size by wall-time and size thresholds)
Implement write-path tagger: attach retention class, legal_hold_id (optional), and minimal provenance metadata at ingestion
Build background pruner process to compact and move data from hot store to escrow tiers per-epoch
Implement rehydration API: authenticated endpoint to pull full context for a given trace with audit token
Integrate audit ledger: append-only access records with requester identity, justification, and TTL for the audit entry
Add RBAC checks: tie rehydration and escrow unlock to role and scope (tenant, org, legal team)
Extend console: retention profile UI, legal-hold management, and rehydration request workflow
Create end-to-end tests and performance benchmarks (ingest latency, rehydration latency, cost delta)
Write runbook for legal/CS on submitting holds and requesting rehydration
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline attaches retention_class and optional legal_hold_id to every telemetry event
Pruner moves >95% of eligible epoch data to escrow within configured window without increasing peak ingest latency by >5%
Rehydration API returns full trace context for a legal_hold_id or approved audit token within SLA (90th percentile < 30s for single-trace requests)
Audit ledger records every rehydration attempt and is queryable by tenant and time range
Console allows product operations to create/expire legal holds and view escrow utilization
Automated tests cover recovery from partial pruner failures and validate no data loss after epoch compaction
decisions: Use compact chunk format (LZ4 + per-chunk AES-GCM) to balance storage cost and rehydration CPU
Epoch boundary aligned to UTC day by default, configurable per-tenant for high-throughput customers
Escrow keys managed via KMS per-tenant with key-rotation workflows; legal-hold unlock requires escrow decryption key held in cold KMS policy
Audit ledger implemented on append-only ledger (immutable store) with weekly snapshotting to prevent tamper
